results.correct_value: At least ~5,300 ft (the row’s own 3,050 ft trailhead to 8,358 ft summit); exact total not settled
results.evidence: The contradiction is real: the row puts the Andrews Creek Trailhead at 3,050 ft and the summit at 8,358 ft, so the car-to-summit gain cannot be below ~5,300 ft. The trailhead elevation (3,050 ft) and the summit elevation (8,358 ft) are confirmed externally, and Andrews Pass is ~6,680 ft at 12 mi. But published gain figures for this approach disagree with each other and none states a car-to-summit total: one gives 4,200-4,600 ft to the lakes, one gives 4,800-7,500 ft to Cathedral Pass depending on route, one gives 6,522 ft for the round trip to the lakes, and the Thirtymile approach is 4,900 ft to the lake. No two sources agree on a single total, so no patch is written.

There are two genuine walk-offs. One source gives the walk east to the saddle, then the trail south and back around to the lake. Another gives the same two options as approach_variants: a short north-side gully about 1,000 ft east of Ka’aba, or a longer loop south around the western arm on trail back to the lake. descent states the trail loop, and approach_variants lists it along with the gully.

results.fact: Approach mileage one-way vs round trip
results.correct_value: ~18-20 miles ONE WAY from the trailhead to Upper Cathedral Lake
results.evidence: The approach to Upper Cathedral Lake is ~18 mi one way from Andrews Creek (40 mi car to car with the summits), ~19 mi one way on the southern approach, and 19.9 mi one way from Thirtymile. results.fact: Route identity: North Buttress vs Middle Finger Buttress Right Side
results.evidence: The published route lists for Amphitheater name only five routes: Pilgrimage to Mecca, Finger of Fatwa, North Ridge, Middle Finger Buttress Left Side and Middle Finger Buttress Right Side. No route called North Buttress is listed. The Right Side is 5.9, 7 pitches, Grade III, FA July 15, 1973, and starts on a steep slab with a thin vertical crack. That matches this row’s fa, face, pitch_detail, pro_tips and itinerary exactly. So this row is very likely a duplicate of the Right Side row with an overview/beta taken from a different description (a line east of the buttress). No source was found for that line, and a route-identity or duplicate question cannot be settled by patching prose. Flagged for a decision on merging or removing it.

results.fact: Finishing pitch: overhanging off-width vs easy 4th class
results.evidence: The Right Side’s published description names only the thin-crack slab start and a short pitch-3 crux, with a “wide range of nuts and cams”. It says nothing about the finish. No source was found for either an overhanging off-width finish or an easy 4th-class last pitch. The off-width claim probably belongs to the separate description the overview was drawn from (see the identity finding), so the finish cannot be settled until the route identity is.
